</figure>
<section id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Task coverage</h5>

<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Benchmarks currently available in BrowserGym cover a broad range of tasks that involve manipulating synthetic UIs (MiniWoB), performing everyday tasks on replicas of real-world shopping, social media, and software development platforms (WebArena, VisualWebArena), executing realistic workflows on an enterprise platform (WorkArena), running time-consuming searches on the open web (AssistantBench), and replicating human interaction traces (WebLINX). For a detailed presentation of each of these benchmarks, we refer the reader to <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Detailed Benchmark Descriptions ‣ The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>. Additional benchmarks currently considered for integration include GAIA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mialon et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, WebVoyager <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">He et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, WebShop <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib65" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yao et al., 2022a</a>)</cite> and Mind2Web-live <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Pan et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Metadata</h5>

<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each BrowserGym benchmark comes with its own metadata, which lists all the available tasks along with their benchmark-specific attributes. For example, the metadata of WorkArena <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Drouin et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Boisvert et al., 2024</a>)</cite> contains the level and the category of each task, which is useful for analyzing the performance of web agents on specific subsets of tasks. The metadata also proposes a default train/test split for each benchmark, and an optional dependency graph between tasks, which indicates a (partial) order in which tasks should be executed to avoid inconsistencies when evaluating agents (e.g., for the WebArena <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib75" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhou et al., 2024b</a>)</cite> and VisualWebArena <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Koh et al., 2024a</a>)</cite> benchmarks).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Suggested evaluation parameters</h5>

<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">On top of the metadata, each BrowserGym benchmark has its own suggested action set, suggested number of seeds per task, and suggested maximum number of steps to be used for evaluation. These suggested parameters are not mandatory but provide a preferred way to evaluate web agents on each benchmark, following the recommendations of the benchmark authors. For example, the MiniWoB(++) benchmark <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib50" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shi et al., 2017</a>; <a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2018</a>)</cite> is not intended to be used in a multiple tab setting, hence does not need the <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">new_tab()</span> or <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">close_tab()</span> action primitives. The AssistantBench benchmark <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib68" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yoran et al., 2024</a>)</cite> on the other hand does not implement task randomization, hence does not need to be evaluated with more than one seed per task.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Backend preparation</h5>

<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Some benchmarks require resetting the backend web server to a specific state before the next agent can be evaluated on it. It is the case for WebArena and VisualWebArena, which require restoring docker containers to their initial state so that any alteration performed by a previous agent (e.g., changing the user’s bio description) is wiped off for the next agent to start in a clean, fresh server state. BrowserGym automates this step with a convenience <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">prepare_backend()</span> routine, which checks the backend configuration (server URL, credentials, etc.) and runs any required reset or setup automatically.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>AgentLab</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As depicted in <a href="#S1.F1" title="In 1 Introduction ‣ The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, AgentLab is a set of tools to simplify experimenting with
agents over BrowserGym. In the high-level API, we define the <span id="S5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">Study</span> object to organize the experiments across multiple agents on a benchmark. The study is materialized on disk and can be launched to run in parallel across multiple processes (<a href="#S5.SS2" title="5.2 Parallel experiments ‣ 5 AgentLab ‣ The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a>). Once a study is completed it can be examined using AgentXRay (<a href="#S5.SS3" title="5.3 AgentXRay ‣ 5 AgentLab ‣ The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.3</span></a>), a custom UI made to introspect the behavior of agents on individual steps of each task in the study. Due to the challenges of reproducing experiments in dynamic environments, we also implement capabilities to help reproducibility (<a href="#S5.SS4" title="5.4 Reproducibility ‣ 5 AgentLab ‣ The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.4</span></a>). Finally, we also provide building blocks to simplify creating new agents (<a href="#S5.SS5" title="5.5 Extensibility: create your own agent ‣ 5 AgentLab ‣ The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.5</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Launching experiments</h3>

<div id="S5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Once an agent is implemented (See <a href="#S5.SS5" title="5.5 Extensibility: create your own agent ‣ 5 AgentLab ‣ The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.5</span></a>), it can be evaluated by creating a <span id="S5.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">Study</span> object and running it:</p>
<div id="S5.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_listing ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting ltx_listing"><div class="ltx_listing_data"><a href="data:text/plain;base64,c3R1ZHkgPSBtYWtlX3N0dWR5KAogICAgYmVuY2htYXJrPSJtaW5pd29iIiwgICMgb3IgIndlYmFyZW5hIiwgIndvcmthcmVuYV9sMSIgLi4uCiAgICBhZ2VudF9hcmdzPVtBR0VOVF80b19NSU5JXSwKKQpzdHVkeS5ydW4obl9qb2JzPTUp" download="">⬇</a></div>
<div id="lstnumberx70" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx70.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">study</span><span id="lstnumberx70.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>=<span id="lstnumberx70.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx70.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">make_study</span>(
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx71" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx71.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">    </span><span id="lstnumberx71.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">benchmark</span>=<span id="lstnumberx71.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_string">"miniwob"</span>,<span id="lstnumberx71.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">  </span><span id="lstnumberx71.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_comment ltx_font_italic">#<span id="lstnumberx71.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>or<span id="lstnumberx71.5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>"webarena",<span id="lstnumberx71.5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>"workarena_l1"<span id="lstnumberx71.5.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>…</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx72" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx72.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">    </span><span id="lstnumberx72.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">agent_args</span>=[<span id="lstnumberx72.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">AGENT_4o_MINI</span>],
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx73" class="ltx_listingline">)
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx74" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx74.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">study</span>.<span id="lstnumberx74.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">run</span>(<span id="lstnumberx74.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">n_jobs</span>=5)
</div>
</div>
<p id="S5.SS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">Study</span> objects are in charge of setting up the experiment and running and saving the reproducibility checks. They also manage the relaunching of failed experiments. In such a broad range of environments, it is frequent to experience system failures such as a server not responding, edge-case bugs in third party libraries, or rate limits from LLM servers. Thus, it is crucial to be able to relaunch failed experiments.
The method <span id="S5.SS1.p1.3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting"><span id="S5.SS1.p1.3.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">Study</span>.<span id="S5.SS1.p1.3.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">run</span></span> is designed to relaunch up to 3 times the failed tasks, but a manual relaunch can also be done as follows:</p>
<div id="S5.SS1.p1.4" class="ltx_listing ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting ltx_listing"><div class="ltx_listing_data"><a href="data:text/plain;base64,c3R1ZHkgPSBTdHVkeS5sb2FkKCIvcGF0aC90by95b3VyL3N0dWR5L2RpciIpCnN0dWR5LmZpbmRfaW5jb21wbGV0ZShpbmNsdWRlX2Vycm9ycz1UcnVlKQpzdHVkeS5ydW4oKQ==" download="">⬇</a></div>
<div id="lstnumberx75" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx75.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">study</span><span id="lstnumberx75.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>=<span id="lstnumberx75.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx75.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">Study</span>.<span id="lstnumberx75.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">load</span>(<span id="lstnumberx75.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_string">"/path/to/your/study/dir"</span>)
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx76" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx76.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">study</span>.<span id="lstnumberx76.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">find_incomplete</span>(<span id="lstnumberx76.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">include_errors</span>=<span id="lstnumberx76.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">True</span>)
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx77" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx77.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">study</span>.<span id="lstnumberx77.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">run</span>()
</div>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>Parallel experiments</h3>

<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Evaluating a single agent on a benchmark with a reasonable number of seeds per task yields several hundred episodes. When exploring multiple agent configurations this can lead to several thousand episodes in a single study. Hence, it is crucial to parallelize efficiently the execution of these episodes.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We use a multiprocess approach with the possibility to use <code id="S5.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">ray</code> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Moritz et al., 2018</a>)</cite> or <code id="S5.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">joblib</code><span id="footnote11" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">11</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">11</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">11</span>
              
              
              
              
              
              
              
            <a href="https://github.com/joblib/joblib" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/joblib/joblib</a></span></span></span> as a backend. Since most of the compute requirements are outsourced to servers (LLM API, TGI server, or web server), the actual compute requirement of the job is relatively small and we can launch up to 20 tasks in parallel on a single laptop or even 50–100 tasks on a server machine with many CPU cores and large memory. With such parallelization, the rate limits of API-based LLMs are usually the bottleneck. If more parallelism is required, <code id="S5.SS2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">ray</code> can connect multiple machines into a single pool of workers. We refer the reader to <a href="#A7" title="Appendix G Experiment runtime and hardware ‣ The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">G</span></a> for further details regarding hardware and runtime.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Task dependencies</h5>

<div id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Benchmarks like (Visual)WebArena have task dependencies to ensure that the execution of a task will not corrupt the instance and prevent it from properly solving other tasks. The <code id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">ray</code> backend is capable of handling such dependencies,<span id="footnote12" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">12</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">12</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">12</span>
                
                
                
                
                
                
                
              <span id="footnote12.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">joblib</span> cannot handle dependency graphs.</span></span></span> but unfortunately this also greatly limits the potential parallelism to 2–4 tasks in parallel for the (Visual)WebArena benchmarks. Also, if the study is created through <span id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">make_study</span>, AgentLab ensures the sequential execution of all agents in the study with a proper instance reset between each evaluation.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.3 </span>AgentXRay</h3>

<div id="S5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To facilitate deeper analysis of agent behavior, AgentLab includes AgentXRay (not be confused with the <code id="S5.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">ray</code> parallel backend), a Gradio-based<span id="footnote13" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">13</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">13</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">13</span>
              
              
              
              
              
              
              
            <a href="https://www.gradio.app" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://www.gradio.app</a></span></span></span> interface for diving deep into the logged traces. A visual example of this interface is shown in Figure <a href="#S5.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ 5.3 AgentXRay ‣ 5 AgentLab ‣ The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>. After selecting the trace of interest AgentXRay displays the profiling, the goal, the different parts of the observation, the action taken, and the prompts, providing a comprehensive view of the agent’s decisions and interactions. This interface allows users to visualize the step-by-step decision-making process of an agent, helping them gain valuable insights and refine their agent for better performance. This is particularly useful for identifying areas where the agent may be struggling, as it allows researchers to pinpoint the exact moment when an incorrect or suboptimal decision is made.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F9" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2412.05467v4/figures/draft7.png" id="S5.F9.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:648/766;" width="648" height="766" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F9.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 9</span>: </span><span id="S5.F9.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Visual rendering of AgentLab’s XRay interface. AgentXRay serves as a powerful analysis tool to inspect and work on BrowserGym agents.
</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.4 </span>Reproducibility</h3>

<div id="S5.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Several factors can influence the reproducibility of results in the context of evaluating agents on dynamic benchmarks. Having a framework robust to the noisy nature of web tasks is necessary. We first discuss core factors that can lead to discrepancies in web agent evaluations and then present the corresponding crucial features that AgentLab implements to mitigate these discrepancies.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS4.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">5.4.1 </span>Factors affecting reproducibility</h4>

<div id="S5.SS4.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS4.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Software version</span>   Different versions of Playwright or any package in the software stack could influence the behavior of the benchmark or the agent. Fixing package versions can help, but it would prevent bug fixes, security updates, and new features.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS4.SSS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">API-based LLMs silently changing</span>   Even for a fixed version, a commercial LLM may be updated, for example, to incorporate the latest web knowledge.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.SSS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.SSS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS4.SSS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Live websites</span>  
Agents that interact with live web content are subject to frequent changes in website design, content availability, and default language settings, which can vary across countries or regions. Websites may update layouts, navigation, or features without notice, disrupting an agent’s performance. Additionally, reliance on dynamic or frequently updated sites introduces unpredictability, as content and structure can shift over time, making consistent evaluation more challenging.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.SSS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.SSS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS4.SSS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Stochastic Agents</span>   LLMs are non-deterministic, but this is less concerning since it is independent and identically distributed (IID) noise, and setting the temperature of the LLM to 0 can reduce most stochasticity.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.SSS1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.SSS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS4.SSS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Non-deterministic tasks</span>  
Similarly, many tasks contain some level of stochasticity. However, changes should be minimal for a fixed seed.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS4.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">5.4.2 </span>Reproducibility Features</h4>

<div id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Standard observation and action space</span>   One core feature of BrowserGym is to provide a standardized observation and action space. While it allows for customization, each benchmark is defined with its own default action space. Similarly, the observation space of agents in AgentLab comes with a default way to represent the DOM, the AXTree, and other components.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Package versions</span>   The <span id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">Study</span> class contains a dictionary of information about reproducibility, including benchmark version, package version, commit hash, os version, and time stamp. By keeping track of these variables, one can isolate package versions, interactions, or system effects that can impact the performance.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reproducibility Journal</span>   A call to <span id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting"><span id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p3.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">study</span>.<span id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p3.1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">append_to_journal</span>()</span> automatically uploads your results to <a href="https://github.com/ServiceNow/AgentLab/blob/main/reproducibility_journal.csv" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting"><span class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">reproducibility_journal</span>.<span class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">csv</span></a>. The goal of this journal is to keep a detailed track of previous results. As mentioned in <a href="#S5.SS4.SSS1" title="5.4.1 Factors affecting reproducibility ‣ 5.4 Reproducibility ‣ 5 AgentLab ‣ The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.4.1</span></a>, because of API changes or instance changes, results can vary overtime.
This makes it easier to populate a large number of reference points. The journal aims to track changes and log enough information to allow anyone to reproduce as closely as possible an experiment. It stores information such as agent name, BrowserGym and AgentLab version, benchmark name and metadata, experiment performances, etc.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reproduced results in the leaderboard</span>   For experiments that are reproducible, we encourage users to try to reproduce the results and upload them to the leaderboard. There is a special column containing information about all reproduced results of an agent on a benchmark. It is displayed as a range of scores alongside the original score on the leaderboard. The leaderboard, together with the Reproducibility Journal, helps monitor changes in benchmarks over time and serves as a source of motivation for the community.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ReproducibilityAgent</span>   The base agent <span id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">GenericAgent</span> (detailed in <a href="#S6" title="6 Experiments ‣ The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>) comes along with an agent called <span id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p5.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">ReproducibilityAgent</span>. Running the latter on an existing study generated from <span id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p5.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">GenericAgent</span> will re-execute the same action sequence on the same task seeds. A visual diff of the two prompts is then displayed in the AgentInfo HTML tab of AgentXray. The user can inspect what changes occurred between the two executions. While the two executions may diverge rapidly if there are some differences at the start of the episode, the diffs between the first few steps are typically insightful on what has changed since the last execution. This allows one to monitor the modifications in live benchmarks that may be subject to changes over time.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.5 </span>Extensibility: create your own agent</h3>

<div id="S5.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At the core, BrowserGym and AgentLab are designed to have a minimalist API for implementing new agents.
Only a few key components need to be implemented in the <span id="S5.SS5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">Agent</span> class:</p>
<div id="S5.SS5.p1.2" class="ltx_listing ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting ltx_listing"><div class="ltx_listing_data"><a href="data:text/plain;base64," download="">⬇</a></div>
<div id="lstnumberx78" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx78.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_bold">class</span><span id="lstnumberx78.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx78.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">MyAgent</span>(<span id="lstnumberx78.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">bgym</span>.<span id="lstnumberx78.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">Agent</span>):
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx79" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx79.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">    </span><span id="lstnumberx79.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_bold">def</span><span id="lstnumberx79.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx79.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">__init__</span>(<span id="lstnumberx79.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">self</span>):
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx80" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx80.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span><span id="lstnumberx80.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_comment ltx_font_italic">#<span id="lstnumberx80.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>define<span id="lstnumberx80.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>an<span id="lstnumberx80.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>action_set<span id="lstnumberx80.2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>to<span id="lstnumberx80.2.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>decode<span id="lstnumberx80.2.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>actions</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx81" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx81.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span><span id="lstnumberx81.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">self</span>.<span id="lstnumberx81.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">action_set</span><span id="lstnumberx81.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>=<span id="lstnumberx81.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx81.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">bgym</span>.<span id="lstnumberx81.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">HighLevelActionSet</span>()
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx82" class="ltx_listingline">
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx83" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx83.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">    </span><span id="lstnumberx83.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_bold">def</span><span id="lstnumberx83.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx83.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">get_action</span>(<span id="lstnumberx83.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">self</span>,<span id="lstnumberx83.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx83.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">obs</span>):
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx84" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx84.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span><span id="lstnumberx84.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_comment ltx_font_italic">#<span id="lstnumberx84.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>the<span id="lstnumberx84.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>core<span id="lstnumberx84.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>of<span id="lstnumberx84.2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>the<span id="lstnumberx84.2.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>agent<span id="lstnumberx84.2.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>reasoning<span id="lstnumberx84.2.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>goes<span id="lstnumberx84.2.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>here</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx85" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx85.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span><span id="lstnumberx85.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_bold">return</span><span id="lstnumberx85.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx85.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">action</span>,<span id="lstnumberx85.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx85.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">agent_info</span>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The main part is the <span id="S5.SS5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">get_action</span> method, where one implements the agent’s logic. It returns an action as a string to be interpreted by BrowserGym, based on the chosen <span id="S5.SS5.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">action_set</span>. The <span id="S5.SS5.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">get_action</span> method can also return <span id="S5.SS5.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">agent_info</span>, an object of type <span id="S5.SS5.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">AgentInfo</span> containing various informations for later inspection of the agent’s behavior.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">AgentArgs</h5>

<div id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">On top of coding an agent, the user is also responsible for coding <span id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">AgentArgs</span>. This is essentially a data structure which the <span id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">make_agent</span> function uses for instantiating an agent. Doing so makes it easy and reliable to pickle experiment information to disk or send it across processes. AgentLab also provides a few other methods for better integration with the framework. For example:</p>
<div id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_listing ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting ltx_listing"><div class="ltx_listing_data"><a href="data:text/plain;base64," download="">⬇</a></div>
<div id="lstnumberx86" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx86.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">@dataclass</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx87" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx87.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_bold">class</span><span id="lstnumberx87.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx87.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">MyAgentArgs</span>(<span id="lstnumberx87.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">agentlab</span>.<span id="lstnumberx87.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">AgentArgs</span>):
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx88" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx88.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">    </span><span id="lstnumberx88.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">use_chain_of_thought</span>:<span id="lstnumberx88.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx88.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_lst_keywords2 ltx_font_bold">bool</span><span id="lstnumberx88.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>=<span id="lstnumberx88.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx88.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">True</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx89" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx89.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">    </span><span id="lstnumberx89.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">use_html</span>:<span id="lstnumberx89.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx89.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_lst_keywords2 ltx_font_bold">bool</span><span id="lstnumberx89.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>=<span id="lstnumberx89.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx89.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">False</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx90" class="ltx_listingline">
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx91" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx91.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">    </span><span id="lstnumberx91.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_bold">def</span><span id="lstnumberx91.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx91.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">make_agent</span>(<span id="lstnumberx91.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">self</span>):<span id="lstnumberx91.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>-&gt;<span id="lstnumberx91.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx91.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">bgym</span>.<span id="lstnumberx91.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">Agent</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx92" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx92.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span><span id="lstnumberx92.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_bold">return</span><span id="lstnumberx92.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx92.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">MyAgent</span>(<span id="lstnumberx92.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">self</span>.<span id="lstnumberx92.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">use_chain_of_thought</span>,<span id="lstnumberx92.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx92.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">self</span>.<span id="lstnumberx92.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">use_html</span>)
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx93" class="ltx_listingline">
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx94" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx94.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">    </span><span id="lstnumberx94.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_bold">def</span><span id="lstnumberx94.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx94.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">set_benchmark</span>(<span id="lstnumberx94.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">self</span>,<span id="lstnumberx94.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx94.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">benchmark</span>):
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx95" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx95.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span><span id="lstnumberx95.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_comment ltx_font_italic">#<span id="lstnumberx95.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>Optional<span id="lstnumberx95.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>method<span id="lstnumberx95.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>to<span id="lstnumberx95.2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>set<span id="lstnumberx95.2.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>benchmark-specific<span id="lstnumberx95.2.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>flags</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx96" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx96.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span><span id="lstnumberx96.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_bold">if</span><span id="lstnumberx96.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx96.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_string">"miniwob"</span><span id="lstnumberx96.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx96.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_bold">in</span><span id="lstnumberx96.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx96.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">benchmark</span>.<span id="lstnumberx96.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">name</span>:
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx97" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx97.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">            </span><span id="lstnumberx97.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">self</span>.<span id="lstnumberx97.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">use_html</span><span id="lstnumberx97.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>=<span id="lstnumberx97.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx97.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">True</span>
</div>
</div>
<p id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Once this is implemented, the user can evaluate their agent as presented in <a href="#S5.SS1" title="5.1 Launching experiments ‣ 5 AgentLab ‣ The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a>. <em id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.3.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Note:</em> the class definition of e.g., <span id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">MyAgentArgs</span> needs to be saved in a module that can be imported from the <span id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">$PYTHONPATH</span> for proper unpickling.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Dynamic Prompting</h5>

<div id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While most modern LLMs can digest more than <math id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100,000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100,000</annotation></semantics></math> tokens, AXTree can still be larger than <math id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100,000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100,000</annotation></semantics></math> tokens, with the raw HTML/DOM counting more than <math id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1,000,000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>000</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1,000,000</annotation></semantics></math> tokens. Additionally, research projects fine-tuning open-source LLMs are often limited to very small context lengths, e.g., <math id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8,000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8,000</annotation></semantics></math>. To manage this, our prompting tools are designed to fit the prompt to the desired length without having to naively truncate the prompt from the end, which would almost always cut crucial information such as examples. This is done using the <span id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">DynamicPrompting</span> class, where the user can easily configure which part of the BrowserGym observation space should be included in the prompt. Next, the length of the prompt is dynamically shrunk to fit a desired size. The <span id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">fit_token</span> method iteratively calls the shrink method recursively on each component of the prompt. Default shrinking strategies are implemented, such as reducing the number of previous steps included in the history, or truncating the page from the bottom. Users can also implement their own shrinking strategies. See <a href="#A3.F11" title="In Appendix C Example Prompt ‣ The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> for a simple example agent using dynamic prompting.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.6 </span>Extensibility: Plug your own LLM / VLM</h3>

<div id="S5.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">AgentLab also offers a base class for LLMs. This allows users to plug their models into any existing agent by just sub-classing our objects. More precisely, we provide a <span id="S5.SS6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">BaseModelArgs</span> class, to configure and log LLM information, as well as instantiating the model, and a <span id="S5.SS6.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">AbstractChatModel</span> class, which just needs a <span id="S5.SS6.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">__call__</span> method defined to query the LLM.
AgentLab comes with different model objects readily available, such as a class for OpenAI models, Azure OpenAI models, or OpenRouter<span id="footnote14" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">14</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">14</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">14</span>
              
              
              
              
              
              
              
            <a href="https://openrouter.ai/" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://openrouter.ai/</a></span></span></span> models. Using our chat model classes allows us to add some useful tools such as a cost and token tracker that can automatically be added to the <span id="S5.SS6.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">AgentInfo</span>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Experiments</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section showcases large-scale experimentation that leverages the BrowserGym ecosystem and evaluates the capabilities of several modern LLMs and VLMs in performing web tasks. We focus on two objectives:</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<ul id="S6.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S6.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">First, showcasing how AgentLab, integrated with BrowserGym, facilitates the creation and management of experiments with web agents.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Second, assessing the current performance levels of various state-of-the-art models in tackling these benchmarks.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S6.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The results of this experiment provide an interesting overview of the strengths and limitations of the evaluated models, offering insights into axes where they require improvements.
The results are consolidated into an online leaderboard, allowing for comparisons and updates as new models and benchmarks emerge.</p>
</div>
<section id="S6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.1 </span>Setup</h3>

<div id="S6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate AgentLab’s default agent, <span id="S6.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">GenericAgent</span>, on all available benchmarks in the BrowserGym ecosystem. <span id="S6.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">GenericAgent</span> employs a modular prompting mechanism that allows it to utilize various tools, such as Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, screenshots with Set-of-Marks (SoM), a memory mechanism, self-criticism, and in-context examples to enhance its responses. The configuration determines both the agent’s behavior and the observation format, including options like using HTML or AXTree representations, retaining a history of observations and past actions, incorporating screenshots or Set-of-Marks images, or displaying additional HTML information from the page.
The <span id="S6.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">ExampleAgent</span> shown in <a href="#A3.F11" title="In Appendix C Example Prompt ‣ The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> in the Appendix gives a simplified overview of our <span id="S6.SS1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">GenericAgent</span>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Along with this dynamic prompting feature, <span id="S6.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">GenericAgent</span> implements a retry functionality to overcome LLM side issues or parsing errors. In the case of a parsing error, the LLM is re-prompted and gets 4 attempts to produce a parsable answer. After 4 consecutive parsing errors, the task is considered a failure.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Our experiments use the same agent configuration as the WorkArena++ benchmark <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Boisvert et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, with the addition of the <span id="S6.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">use_think_history</span> setting which gives the agent access to its entire chain-of-thought history throughout its execution, similarly to <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">Putta et al. (2024)</a></cite>. Intuitively, this allows the agent to remember previous interactions and outcomes, and make more informed and consistent decisions. An example of a resulting prompt is showcased in <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Example Prompt ‣ The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate AgentLab’s <span id="S6.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">GenericAgent</span> using a representative subset of state-of-the-art large language models, which includes:</p>
<ul id="S6.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S6.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">GPT-4o</span> and <span id="S6.I2.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">GPT-4o Mini</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">OpenAI, 2024a</a>)</cite> using the Azure OpenAI API, as some of the best models available on the market. We use respectively checkpoints <span id="S6.I2.i1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">2024-08-06</span> and <span id="S6.I2.i1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">2024-07-18</span>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">o1 Mini</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">OpenAI, 2024b</a>)</cite> using the OpenRouter API, to test out the performances of test-time reasoning-focused models. We use the <span id="S6.I2.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">2024-09-12</span> checkpoint for this model.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Claude 3.5 Sonnet</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Anthropic, 2024a</a>)</cite> using the OpenRouter API, as the best-performing model on our benchmarks. We use the <span id="S6.I2.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">2024-10-22</span> checkpoint, most recent to this day.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I2.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I2.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I2.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I2.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Llama-3.1</span> 70B and 405B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Meta, 2024</a>)</cite> using the OpenRouter API, as representatives of the open-weights LLM community, to assess their performance relative to their proprietary counterparts and identify improvement axes.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">As our evaluation metric, we use the task success rate, i.e. the percentage of tasks that were successfully completed by the agent, and compute the standard error (<math id="S6.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma/\sqrt{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>/</mo><msqrt><mi>N</mi></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma/\sqrt{N}</annotation></semantics></math>). We evaluate our agent with all the previously mentioned LLMs, on all benchmarks, with some exceptions. On WorkArena L3, except for Claude, we report results obtained in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Boisvert et al. (2024)</a></cite> as they are similar agents and we have strong expectations that the score would not change, leading to significant resource savings. On VisualWebArena, we only run the LLMs that support multi-modal inputs. Out of fairness between models, we do not use visual inputs for the other benchmarks, as they do not require it.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS1.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A5.T5" title="In Appendix E Benchmark setting ‣ The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> in the Appendix shows the settings used for each benchmark and the number of evaluation tasks for each. Indeed the number of tasks (or episodes) depends on the number of seeds (MiniWob, WorkArena L1), or the split used. We use the test splits for WebLINX and AssistantBench. Finally, WorkArena L2 and L3 offer their own curricula, amounting to 235 tasks each.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.2 </span>Results</h3>

<figure id="S6.T2" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S6.T2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 2</span>: </span><span id="S6.T2.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Results of a full round of experimentation on the unified benchmark ecosystem. The # Ep. column indicates the number of evaluation episodes per benchmark, which depends on the number of tasks and seeds used (See <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Benchmark setting ‣ The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a> for details). For budget reasons, grayed-out values (<span id="S6.T2.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">0.0</span>) indicate skipped evaluations for the least-performing models on the hardest benchmark (WorkArena L3). The table also shows the total cost (USD) and average step per episode for the overall best-performing model, Claude 3.5 Sonnet. Costs for each LLM are given in <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Costs and API Usage ‣ The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a> along with API cost details.</span></figcaption>

<td id="S6.T2.6.10.16" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb"><math id="S6.T2.m101" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn mathsize="0.800em">7.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7.5</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>

</table>
</figure>
<div id="S6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We present the results obtained using various open-source and closed-source LLMs as <span id="S6.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_lst_language_python ltx_lstlisting">GenericAgent</span>s across standard web agent benchmarks in <a href="#S6.T2" title="In 6.2 Results ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>. We observe that Claude obtains the best performance across the majority of the benchmarks, with o1-Mini falling second. Claude surprisingly improves substantially over the previously unsolved WorkArena-L2 benchmark and obtains an average task success rate of 39.1%. One explanation for this impressive result could be Claude’s specific training for computer use <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Anthropic, 2024b</a>)</cite>, which bears a close resemblance to using a web browser. We also observe that Llama-3.1 70B obtains very close performance to GPT-4o Mini, and Llama-3.1-405B surpasses GPT-4o-Mini significantly on numerous benchmarks. While beaten on most complex reasoning benchmarks, 405B still obtains more than decent performances overall, which comes as a promising omen for the open-source community.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We also observe an improvement in performance for GPT-4o compared to the performance measured by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Boisvert et al. (2024)</a></cite>, which goes from <math id="S6.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="23.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>23.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">23.5\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S6.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="31.4\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>31.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">31.4\%</annotation></semantics></math> on WebArena, and from <math id="S6.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.8\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.8</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.8\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S6.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>8.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.5\%</annotation></semantics></math> on WorkArena L2. Since they were using a very similar web agent implementation but an older model checkpoint, this suggests that the reasoning capabilities of GPT-4o have greatly increased thanks to the additional training performed for this new checkpoint. Another option to explain this improvement might be the public availability of those benchmarks and their support, meaning parts of their content might now be integrated into some form in the LLM pre-training / fine-tuning datasets.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">One interesting point is that our agent seems to underperform on AssistantBench, a web-based question-answering benchmark. Our best agent attains a score of <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6.9\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6.9</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.9\%</annotation></semantics></math>, which is a very low score compared to the current high score of <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="27\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>27</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">27\%</annotation></semantics></math> on the AssistantBench leaderboard.
Our agent is not specifically optimized for information retrieval tasks, which are the primary focus of the AssistantBench benchmark. Instead, our API and agent are designed to be broadly applicable across a wide range of web-based tasks, prioritizing generality over specialization.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.3 </span>Errors</h3>

<div id="S6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">When evaluating AI agents, errors can generally be classified into a few broad categories. <span id="S6.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Navigation Errors</span> occur when the agent struggles to locate the correct page or information, often due to poor search queries or navigation mistakes. <span id="S6.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Form Handling Errors</span> involve incorrect data entry, such as formatting issues or failure to recognize submission failures. <span id="S6.SS3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Task Understanding Errors</span> arise when an agent misinterprets unclear instructions, leading to irrelevant or incorrect actions. <span id="S6.SS3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Stuck Behavior</span> happens when an agent repeats the same failing action without adapting to the situation. <span id="S6.SS3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Information Extraction Failures</span> occur when the agent successfully navigates to the right location but fails to correctly extract, interpret, or return the necessary data. Finally, <span id="S6.SS3.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">External Errors</span> stem from technical issues such as API failures, network errors, or system crashes that hinder the agent’s performance. While these categories are not definitive, they offer a useful framework for diagnosing weaknesses and improving AI agent reliability.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Given the scale of our experiments, we only provide a qualitative overview of the errors encountered by the agent. However, we release the full traces of our experiments and let to the reader the possibility to skim through the data using AgentXRay. <a href="#A8" title="Appendix H Results analysis ‣ The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H</span></a> showcases a detailed description of the trace from two models on the same task. This succinct analysis suggests that Claude exhibits a degree of robustness, as it is able to recover from past errors. Future work will focus on conducting a deeper analysis of Web Agent errors and developing automated methods for such evaluations.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Discussion</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this work, we introduced the BrowserGym ecosystem, which contributes to the standardization of web agent research by providing a unified environment for evaluating web agents. We make our contribution available as two easy-to-use Python packages, BrowserGym and AgentLab. The first provides a unified platform exposing all existing web agent benchmarks under the same interface, and is designed to facilitate the addition of new benchmarks. AgentLab, on the other hand, provides a complementary interface and set of tools for the implementation and evaluation of web agents, with a set of flexible web agent implementations, an expandable LLM / VLM API, reproducibility features, trace analysis tools, as well as an online leaderboard.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To showcase our main contribution, we conducted the first large-scale empirical evaluation of a representative set of state-of-the-art LLM / VLM models on six popular web agent benchmarks, using AgentLab and BrowserGym. While running such an experiment using the original, fragmented benchmark codes would be extremely cumbersome, BrowserGym makes all of them accessible through the same interface and allows for large-scale, unified experiments in a single code base with AgentLab. By fostering reproducibility and facilitating consistent benchmarks, the BrowserGym ecosystem lays the groundwork for more dependable and insightful evaluations of web agent capabilities, thus accelerating the advancement of LLM-driven automation.</p>
</div>
<section id="S7.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.1 </span>Limitations</h3>

<section id="S7.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Reproducibility</h5>

<div id="S7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Despite our efforts to improve reproducibility, stochasticity, and external factors remain significant challenges. Localization differences, such as time zones, default languages, and geographic settings, can lead to inconsistent agent behaviors when interacting with live websites. Additionally, variations in operating systems and browsers can affect how web pages are rendered, impacting the uniformity of results. The presence of dynamic elements, such as advertisements, adds to non-determinism, leading agents to face different environments during repeated tasks, which affects their consistency. Addressing these challenges is essential for reliable and repeatable benchmarks in web agent research.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Risks</h5>

<div id="S7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Letting an autonomous agent act on the world-wide-web on a human’s behalf can have consequences, and prove to be problematic on benchmarks that require an open-web access (AssistantBench, soon GAIA). This is currently mitigated in BrowserGym via URL protection (MiniWoB, WorkArena, WebArena / VisualWebArena), plus a warning notice on BrowserGym and AgentLab’s landing pages.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Robot detection</h5>

<div id="S7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Robot detection mechanisms significantly limit web agents, especially for open-web tasks. Websites use techniques like CAPTCHA, IP rate limiting, and behavior analysis to block automated agents, preventing them from completing tasks effectively. This limits the ability of agents to interact freely with web environments and reduces the scope of tasks that can be automated. AssistantBench is the only benchmark impacted by those issues so far in BrowserGym, as it uses the open web as its information retrieval tool.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS1.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Agent collisions</h5>

<div id="S7.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The widespread use of databases on the web means that many tasks involve updating records and modifying entries. When multiple agents operate simultaneously, they can interfere with each other, especially when executing tasks that alter the same database entries. For example, if two agents add an item to their cart concurrently, they may unintentionally update each other’s cart, leading to inconsistent outcomes. This issue is particularly problematic in environments like WebArena and VisualWebArena, where a single virtual machine is used for each agent. As a result, only one agent can be run at a time on these benchmarks, significantly slowing down the evaluation process.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS1.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Synchronous interactions</h5>

<div id="S7.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Another limitation is the sync loop mechanism used to manage interactions within the browser environment. For example, when agents need to perform multiple actions in quick succession, the sync loop may not keep up, leading to delays and reduced efficiency. This can result in performance bottlenecks, especially for complex tasks requiring rapid, sequential actions.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.2 </span>Avenue for Future Work</h3>

<div id="S7.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To further develop the field, several areas require attention. One promising direction is improving <span id="S7.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">safety</span> mechanisms for web agents. Currently, safety evaluation in web agent benchmarks, including ensuring agents’ compliance with data privacy and safety policies, as well as their resilience to malicious interactions, is underexplored. The development of secure environments is crucial for adopting web agents in enterprise or sensitive applications.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Another avenue for future work involves the creation of real-time web agents capable of interacting with live environments at speeds comparable to human users. This necessitates improvements in both latency reduction and real-time decision-making, which would enhance the applicability of web agents in dynamic settings, such as customer service or rapid data retrieval.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The potential for smaller, yet efficient LLMs is also an important focus. Developing smaller models that retain the ability to understand and reason through complex web interactions would lower computational demands, making web automation more accessible and sustainable. This aligns with efforts to increase the efficiency of LLM-based agents, particularly for real-world deployment where computational resources may be constrained.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">In addition, enhancing reactivity through the use of computer-level vision-language models (VLMs) can provide agents with a more nuanced understanding of the visual context on web pages. Current models often lack the capability to fully interpret complex visual layouts or graphical information, limiting their interaction fidelity with certain websites. Integrated models like Anthropic’s computer use model could make web agents more versatile and capable of handling tasks that require both visual reasoning and textual inputs.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Another direction is to leverage inference time scaling, optimizing it specifically for web tasks and web agents. This could involve making better use of the model’s self-reflection capabilities to further improve task performance, adapting dynamically to various complexities encountered during web navigation, and efficiently managing resources to reduce latency. By tailoring these improvements, web agents can become more effective at real-time, adaptive decision-making, ultimately enhancing user experiences and broadening their applicability.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">As BrowserGym saves and logs every piece of information seen in its experiments, it could serve as a valuable collection tool for finetuning models. This collected data could be utilized to further refine agent behaviors, improve model performance on specific web tasks, and create efficient agents capable of handling complex scenarios more efficiently.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S8" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">8 </span>Broader Impact</h2>

<div id="S8.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The development of more general UI-based agents holds the potential to significantly transform how work is performed on computers. These agents promise to automate tasks at an unprecedented pace, with reduced costs, and with a broader and deeper scope of expertise. While current benchmarks demonstrate that this level of sophistication has not yet been achieved, the rapid pace of advancements in the field suggests that such a future may not be far off. This progress could unlock immense economic value but is also likely to result in substantial and rapid job displacement, presenting a critical societal challenge.</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S8.p2.1" class="ltx_p">AI safety must be central to this emerging agentic revolution. Presently, jailbreaking a large language model (LLM) might only expose knowledge already available on the web. However, as agents become more sophisticated, vulnerabilities such as prompt-injection attacks could be exploited to leak sensitive company information, authorize unwanted transactions, or cause other unintended harm. The widespread deployment of agents at scale will create enormous financial incentives for malicious actors to develop targeted attacks that uncover and exploit weaknesses in these systems.</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S8.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The rise of UI-based agents also introduces new challenges and considerations regarding digital advertising. As these agents navigate the web autonomously, their interactions with dynamic ad content could disrupt existing advertising models, impacting both advertisers and publishers. Unlike human users, agents are unlikely to engage with ads in traditional ways, which may lead to shifts in how ad impressions, clicks, and conversions are measured and monetized. Additionally, the ability of agents to filter, block, or bypass advertisements could create conflicts with current web monetization strategies. To maintain a fair and functional digital ecosystem, actors from both sides should explore standardized approaches for handling ad-related content in a way that balances automation efficiency with the sustainability of online advertisement business models.</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S8.p4.1" class="ltx_p">As these technologies evolve, society must proactively address the accompanying challenges by establishing robust policies and frameworks. Rapid action will be essential to ensure that the benefits of these advancements are maximized while minimizing potential risks and harm.</p>
</div>
</section>

<div id="lstnumberx126" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx126.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">    </span><span id="lstnumberx126.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">Description</span>:<span id="lstnumberx126.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx126.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">Notifies</span><span id="lstnumberx126.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx126.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">the</span><span id="lstnumberx126.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx126.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">user</span><span id="lstnumberx126.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx126.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">that</span><span id="lstnumberx126.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx126.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">their</span><span id="lstnumberx126.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx126.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">instructions</span><span id="lstnumberx126.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx126.16" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">are</span><span id="lstnumberx126.17" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx126.18" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">infeasible</span>.
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx127" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx127.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">    </span><span id="lstnumberx127.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">Examples</span>:
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx128" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx128.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span><span id="lstnumberx128.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">report_infeasible</span>(<span id="lstnumberx128.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_string">’I<span id="lstnumberx128.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">␣</span>cannot<span id="lstnumberx128.3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">␣</span>follow<span id="lstnumberx128.3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">␣</span>these<span id="lstnumberx128.3.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">␣</span>instructions<span id="lstnumberx128.3.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">␣</span>because<span id="lstnumberx128.3.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">␣</span>there<span id="lstnumberx128.3.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">␣</span>is<span id="lstnumberx128.3.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">␣</span>no<span id="lstnumberx128.3.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">␣</span>email<span id="lstnumberx128.3.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">␣</span>field<span id="lstnumberx128.3.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">␣</span>in<span id="lstnumberx128.3.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">␣</span>this<span id="lstnumberx128.3.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">␣</span>form.’</span>)
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx129" class="ltx_listingline">
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx130" class="ltx_listingline">…
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx131" class="ltx_listingline">
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx132" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx132.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">Only</span><span id="lstnumberx132.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx132.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">a</span><span id="lstnumberx132.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx132.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">single</span><span id="lstnumberx132.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx132.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">action</span><span id="lstnumberx132.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx132.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">can</span><span id="lstnumberx132.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx132.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">be</span><span id="lstnumberx132.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx132.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">provided</span><span id="lstnumberx132.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx132.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">at</span><span id="lstnumberx132.16" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx132.17" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">once</span>.<span id="lstnumberx132.18" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx132.19" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">Example</span>:
